title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Top Support Issues (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s canonical approach for developer-facing documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to provide a single, opinionated reference for writers, engineers, and support to ensure consistent, high-quality developer experience content that reduces time-to-first-success for new users and lowers support volume.

Audience:
- Developer Experience (DevEx) writers
- SDK owners and contributors
- Support engineers and solutions specialists
- Product and platform engineers who ship APIs

Owners and SLAs:
- Primary owner: DevEx (engineering)
- Engineering contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Support contact: Miguel Santos (support-ux@redwood.ai)
- Docs publishing SLA: changes to published quickstarts must be reviewed and merged within 5 business days for high-impact fixes; emergency patches (security / breaking API change) within 24 hours.

Standards and Conventions (required):
1) Structure for SDK Guides and Quickstarts
   - Title: concise, action-oriented (e.g., "Python Quickstart: Text Generation")
   - Short intro (1–2 sentences): goal and expected outcome
   - Prerequisites: account, API key, minimal environment (OS, python/node version)
   - Install (copy/paste commands)
   - Minimal example (runnable in < 30s)
   - Expand: auth, advanced options, streaming, error handling
   - Troubleshooting: 3 most common errors and fixes
   - Copyable code blocks and curl examples
   - Links: SDK reference, API reference, related quickstarts, and issue tracker

2) File naming and frontmatter
   - File name: kebab-case, short (e.g., python-quickstart-text-generation-2026.json)
   - Metadata block in page JSON: title, author, created_at, last_updated, labels, reviewers, status (as present on this page)

3) Code & Example Policies
   - All examples must be runnable without client libraries (provide curl) and with the official SDKs (Python, NodeJS).
   - Avoid long model names in examples; use aliases from the model catalog (e.g., "redwood/text-1") and include a note if alias may change.
   - Do not include production API keys in examples. Use REDWOOD_API_KEY env var pattern.

Example Quickstart: Python Text Generation (copyable)
1) Prerequisites
   - Python 3.10+
   - pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0
   - REDWOOD_API_KEY set in environment

2) Install
   - pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0

3) Minimal example
   ```python
   from redwood import RedwoodClient
   import os

   client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))

   resp = client.generate(
       model='redwood/text-1',
       prompt='Write a haiku about distributed systems',
       max_tokens=60,
   )
   print(resp.text)
   ```

4) Curl equivalent
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood/text-1","prompt":"Write a haiku about distributed systems","max_tokens":60}'
   ```

5) Advanced topics (links to deeper pages)
   - Streaming responses: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/streaming-responses
   - Tool/Function calling patterns: /confluence/product-docs/requirements/function-calling-patterns
   - Embeddings quickstart: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/embeddings-quickstart-2025

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publishing workflow)
- Branching: create topic branch under docs-site repo: docs/<space>/<short-title>
- PR template: include links to rendered preview, test instructions, and SLO impact (if any).
- Reviewers: add at least one DevEx writer + SDK owner for code examples.
- CI checks: linting (markdownlint), code sample execution (pytest for python snippets, node-tap for JS snippets), link-checker.
- Staging: merged PRs are deployed to docs-staging.redwood.ai automatically; QA must sign off within 48 hours before promoting.
- Promotion: for content-only changes, promotion to production occurs on daily deploy window (03:00 UTC). For breaking fixes, use emergency deploy procedures in runbook "docs-emergency-patch".

On-call and Escalation for Docs-related Incidents
1) If customer reports broken example / wrong API behavior: support engineer files an internal issue with label "docs-bug" and assigns to DevEx.
2) If example causes production traffic spikes (e.g., runaway loop), escalate to SDK owner and eng-sre. Use priority P1 if customer impact is high.
3) Communication: add a short banner to affected docs and a note in status page until fix is merged.

Top 10 Support Issues (canonical fixes) — canonical fixes must be copy-paste ready
1) "401 Unauthorized" on curl examples
   - Cause: missing/invalid REDWOOD_API_KEY or mis-typed header
   - Detection: request/response logs show 401 with X-Request-Id
   - Fix: ensure header 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' is present; verify key using `redwood-cli auth whoami`
   - Short fix snippet: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(redwood-cli auth token)`

2) Slow responses for short prompts (high latency)
   - Cause: client using high-latency model variant or not using streaming for large outputs
   - Fix: recommend 'redwood/text-low-latency' for short outputs; enable streaming or reduce max_tokens; provide batching guidance in Optimize toolkit link

3) SDK install fails on older pip / node versions
   - Cause: unsupported Python/version mismatch
   - Fix: update to Python 3.10+ or use pyenv: `pyenv install 3.10.12 && pyenv local 3.10.12`

4) Mismatched response shapes between SDK and HTTP API
   - Cause: SDK version out-of-sync with API contract
   - Fix: pin SDK to recommended version in quickstart: `pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0` and reference changelog page

5) Streaming examples not reconnecting after network hiccup
   - Cause: client lacks reconnect/backoff logic
   - Fix: show example backoff pseudocode and use official SDK reconnect helpers (redwood.streaming.backoff)

6) Embeddings dimensionality mismatch in customer code
   - Cause: mixing legacy and v2 embedding model outputs
   - Fix: map dimensionality in code and recommend `redwood/embeddings-v2` in quickstarts; include sample normalization code

7) Rate limit 429 errors during load testing
   - Cause: client performing synchronous retries without backoff
   - Fix: implement exponential backoff; advise use of batching and Dedication for high throughput; sample retry header parsing provided

8) Local dev environment can't reach private deployment (VPC)
   - Cause: missing VPN / firewall rules or wrong base URL in environment
   - Fix: verify VPC tunnel, ensure REDWOOD_API_BASE is pointed to private endpoint; provide curl for endpoint check: `curl -v $REDWOOD_API_BASE/health`

9) Tokenization surprises (unexpected token counts)
   - Cause: misunderstanding of tokenizer / whitespace handling
   - Fix: include token counting snippet in quickstarts: `from redwood.tokenizer import count_tokens` and show examples with emojis and unicode

10) Mismatched model alias after rollout
   - Cause: model alias moved to new underlying variant during canary rollouts
   - Fix: include model pinning example: `model: redwood/text-1@2026-01-12` and instructions for pinning in Dedicated/Private deployments

Canonical Fix Template (must be included with every support doc)
- Symptom: <one-line description>
- Cause: <short root cause>
- Diagnostic steps (1–3): commands to run or logs to check
- Fix (copy/paste): commands/code to apply
- Owner: team and individual contact
- Rollback: steps to revert change if needed

Checklist for Quickstarts before publishing (author must verify):
- [ ] Minimal example runs in <30s locally and in CI
- [ ] Curl + SDK examples included and produce equivalent outputs
- [ ] Prereqs documented and pinned versions included
- [ ] Troubleshooting section includes at least 3 issues
- [ ] Reviewed and approved by SDK owner
- [ ] Labels and related_pages set for discoverability

Template: Minimum Quickstart JSON frontmatter (copy into new docs)
{
  "title": "<short-title>",
  "space": "eng-developer-experience",
  "author": "<author name>",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "draft",
  "created_at": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "labels": ["quickstart","sdk"],
  "content": "<document body goes here>"
}

Maintenance and audit
- Quarterly audit: DevEx will run a script to verify that all quickstarts render and that code snippets pass smoke tests. Failures create issues with label "docs-audit-fix".
- Deprecation: If an SDK version is EOL, add deprecation banner 60 days before removal and update affected pages.

Appendix: Useful commands and test harnesses
- Run Python snippet tests: `pytest tests/snippets/python -q`
- Run JS snippet tests: `npm run test:snippets`
- Lint docs: `npm run lint:docs`
- Preview docs locally: `npm run dev` (serves on http://localhost:3000)
